summary: The read-only enforcement diffs git-status snapshots that an agent RETURNS; the workflow DSL has only phase/agent/parallel/log/args globals (no fs/child_process), so there is no out-of-band filesystem observer. A shard that forges its returned output — including the degenerate case of returning two empty/identical well-formed snapshots, which diff to an empty delta = PASS — can evade detection. Malformed manifest-read and malformed combine-input ARE fail-closed, but an empty-but-well-formed snapshot pair is not separately guarded.
evidence: Proposal: 'Snapshot transport remains within the platform's existing agent/tool trust boundary ... not cryptographic proof an agent process cannot forge its own output', and Risks 'Snapshot forgery / concurrent unrelated writers ... mechanical adjudication within the existing agent/tool trust boundary, not a cryptographic attestation' (mitigations: raw git-status retention in the artifact + single-driver discipline + independent wiring audit). Plan L134: inline DSL _diffAuditSnapshotLines runs on the RETURNED raw snapshot strings, raw output retained as the auditability backstop; Plan L102: takeGitSnapshot/execFileSync live in composite-audit.ts (run by an agent), not the DSL. DSL no-import/no-fs fact grounded in execute-milestone.js L24 globals. This is an explicitly disclosed, architecturally inherent accepted limitation (no stronger in-architecture mechanism exists), resolved by disclosure + mitigations rather than left unresolved — hence non-blocking.
claimRef: Proposal 'Chosen mechanism' para 4 ('The workflow itself ... diffs the two snapshots') + 'Risks and mitigations' (Snapshot forgery)
